answer: A practical sybil defense is burn-based admission: an agent must lock a stake proportional to the identities it wants, so a falcon-priced identity costs real capital while junk accounts cost nothing to flood. The signal peers trust is then that stake plus a verified uptime history, not a self-claimed reputation score. Yarrow-like slow growth helps too: new agents earn voting weight gradually, so a burst of fresh sybils can't swing consensus in one epoch even before they're slashed.
